"Karthik, you can't even boil an egg? Seriously?" Sahil laughed, loud enough for the cousins in the hall to hear. "My brother, the genius."
Karthik put the pan down and walked out. The cousins went quiet.
Later, Papa found Sahil on the balcony. "That was the third time today."
"He's lazy, Papa. He sleeps till ten. He never studies. And everyone still loves him."
"Hmm. And what bothers you most about that?"
"Nothing. I just think he's useless."
Papa waited.
"Fine," Sahil muttered. "He gets to be easy-going and I have to be the serious one. I'm scared if I relax for one day, I'll fall behind. And he never seems scared of anything."
"So it's not really about eggs."
Sahil laughed, but it came out wrong. "No." He looked through the glass at Karthik, alone with his phone. "He doesn't talk to me anymore. I guess I did that."

qa.a: On the balcony.

qa.q: What was Sahil really feeling beneath the insults?
qa.a: He felt envious of Karthik's easy-going life and afraid of falling behind if he ever relaxed.

qa.q: What would you advise Sahil to do next?
qa.a: Apologise to Karthik, especially for mocking him in front of the cousins, and try talking to him about something he likes instead of criticising.

qa.q: How does Karthik likely see Sahil's jokes?
qa.a: To Karthik they feel humiliating, especially in front of the cousins, so he walks out and has stopped talking to his brother.

grounding: A teen who calls his brother useless realises contempt has shut down their closeness and that it hides his own envy and fear.

Her first thought was Pooja didi. Didi had paid the fees for this whole year from her first salary at the bank, without being asked. Every time Shalini opened a textbook she felt grateful, and also the weight of it. What if she didn't get in? What if all that money just vanished?

In the corridor she took out her phone. It rang twice.
"Didi? Rank 212. I wanted you to know first. And thank you, properly. I don't say it because I'm scared of letting you down."
Pooja was quiet, then laughed shakily. "Silly. I paid so you could try, not so you'd owe me."

Friday night
I did something today I'm not proud of.
At lunch everyone was bored, and Kanika said, "Nirmala, you always know stuff. Tell us something." And I did. I told them Yamini's family moved because her father's shop closed. Yamini told me that at her house, weeks ago.
For about five minutes it felt amazing. Everyone leaned in. Someone said, "No way!" I felt like the most interesting person at the table.
Then Yamini walked into the canteen. The table went quiet in that awful way, and she knew. She turned right around.
I've been sick about it all evening. I basically bought five minutes of being popular with Yamini's worst secret.
Tomorrow I'll tell Yamini the truth and say sorry. And the next time Kanika asks me for "something," I'm going to say I've got nothing.

qa.q: Who asked Nirmala to tell something at lunch?
qa.a: Kanika.

qa.q: How did Nirmala feel before and after Yamini walked in?
qa.a: Nirmala felt thrilled and interesting at first, then guilty and sick once Yamini's face showed she knew.

qa.q: What does Nirmala plan to do next time, and why is it wise?
qa.a: Nirmala plans to refuse to share gossip with Kanika, which stops trading someone else's pain for attention.

qa.q: What was it like for Yamini when she entered the canteen?
qa.a: Yamini felt exposed and hurt, sensing that everyone knew, so she turned right around.

grounding: A teen passes on a friend's secret for a moment of belonging, feels the thrill then guilt, and resolves to stop.
